clue.text: Mercenary spies Jack among fringe characters

indicators.note: among places the card letter amid the other piece, which surrounds it

parts.note: a Nina is a message a setter hides in a grid, typically around its edges, so these are characters on the fringe
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Hired agents slip a man called Jack in among people on the margins of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe characters' looks like eccentrics; it is the crossword term NINAS, grid-edge messages, with J placed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninja were Japanese agents hired for espionage and assassination.

clue.text: Ugly heads holding nameless drink removed from picture

indicators.note: holding means the outer letters keep the drink inside them
ugly suggests something misshapen, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nameless tells us to drop N, the abbreviation for name, from the drink

parts.note: Irn-Bru is a Scottish fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant characters are clutching an unidentified beverage before being cut from a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ugly heads' reads as unpleasant people, but 'Ugly' is the anagram signal giving A SHED; 'holding' puts the drink, minus N by 'nameless', inside. Irn-Bru is a famous Scottish soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush someone is to edit an image so they vanish from it.

clue.text: Geordieland's message to Queen (group)

parts.note: Geordies come from Tyneside in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
a word is a brief message, as in 'send word'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Tyneside sends a note to the monarch, with an aside about a band.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(group)' is the definition: the Manchester band of 'Blue Monday' fame. 'Geordieland' is Newcastle and Tyneside.
explanation.definitionFit: New Order are an English rock band formed from Joy Division.

clue.text: Satellite dish essentially needing a little readjustment

annotationWithheld.why: Satellite dish essentially needing a little readjustment (6): the only parse anagrams EEDIN (core of 'needing') plus R, the first letter of 'readjustment', so 'readjustment' is both the anagram indicator and the source of R
annotationWithheld.clue: Satellite dish essentially needing a little readjustment

clue.text: Roguish lord shows no hesitation

indicators.note: shows no tells us the peer's name loses the sound of faltering

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and politician, sits in the Lords as Lord Archer
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A mischievous peer speaks without faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: The lord is Jeffrey Archer, the British novelist made a life peer; drop ER and ARCH is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, mischievous manner, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Doctor — one into cooking pasta

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig or tamper with them
a means one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying them, so the next word's letters are cooked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic, someone keen on making food, is preparing pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medic but is the verb, rig; 'cooking' rearranges INTO to TONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are short, ridged tubes of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Cooking is popular — stick around

indicators.note: around says the snooker stick wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a cue is a snooker or billiards stick
taken as written
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Food preparation is in fashion, so keep at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' reads as 'stay', but the snooker stick is wrapped around the other pieces by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cookery, as in French cuisine.

clue.text: Politician opposed to welcoming Obama maybe? Not half

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for 'against' takes the other piece inside

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against

indicators.note: not half tells us to keep only the first four of the eight letters

parts.note: Barack Obama is an example of an American

explanation.surface: A party figure hostile to receiving a US president, perhaps not wholeheartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obama maybe' gives AMERICAN, which 'Not half' cuts to AMER; CON holds it. David Cameron was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron was UK prime minister and Conservative leader.

clue.text: Actress Liz's pronouncement on EastEnders shifts

indicators.note: a pronouncement in a Cockney accent, like the East End soap, drops the H at the start

parts.note: Liz Hurley is an English actress and model

explanation.surface: A film star's remark on the BBC soap set in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, where Cockneys drop their aitches: 'Hurley's' becomes ''urley's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlies are early work shifts, as opposed to lates.

clue.text: Paper features 'It' girl

indicators.note: features means the newspaper contains the other piece

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
SA, sex appeal, is old slang for 'it', as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a story about a glamorous young socialite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal is SA, an old crossword convention; it goes inside SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a girl's name.

clue.text: Gang keeps egghead in low-paid work

indicators.note: keeps means the gang holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a mob is a gang of criminals
CJ de Mooi was one of the quiz champions on the BBC show Eggheads

explanation.surface: A criminal gang holds an intellectual captive in a menial job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' is not just a brainbox: it is CJ de Mooi from the BBC quiz show Eggheads.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is a dead-end, poorly paid service job, from fast-food work.

clue.text: Not right — ever so hard fiddling expenses

indicators.note: fiddling suggests tinkering, so these words are rearranged once the letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Wrong to fiddle your expenses so blatantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes one R from EVER SO HARD; 'fiddling' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheads are a business's regular running costs.

clue.text: Programme endorsed around university was widely known

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the other piece
to programme is to arrange, so the letters of the next word are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV show backed by a university campus became famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programme' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal: ENDORSED becomes RESONDED, which goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resounded rang out far and wide, so was widely celebrated or known.

clue.text: Depressed about river flood

indicators.note: about means the low mood wraps the other piece

parts.note: down means depressed or low

explanation.surface: A gloomy riverside resident fears inundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown a field is to flood or submerge it.

clue.text: Losing bottle finally, put off fight — that's slander

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the deterring word

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word bottle

parts.note: action is fighting, as in seeing action

explanation.surface: Losing nerve, someone postpones a bout; others call them names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing bottle' looks like lost courage; it drops E (bottle's last letter) from DETER to leave DETR.
explanation.definitionFit: Detraction is the belittling of someone's reputation, a form of defamation.

clue.text: Nightwear's on the ground — that's surprising

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters are remade into new words

parts.note: taken as written, with the S counted
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pyjamas left lying on the floor provoke an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the floor, but it is the past tense of grind: an anagram signal for NIGHTWEARS plus ON THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation meaning 'well, fancy that'.

clue.text: Tries to persuade with flattery — wife's mostly taking no notice

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: heedless means paying no attention

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes and sweet-talks, though their wife largely ignores them.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax with flattery and charm.

clue.text: Coe's planned to take in country over proposed development

indicators.note: to take in means the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
planned means arranged, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written, with the S counted

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Seb Coe's strategy for absorbing a nation's influence over a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned' looks like Seb Coe's scheme but rearranges the letters of 'Coe's'; 'over' turns the country backwards in this down clue, and 'to take in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a projected sequence of events, a possible development.

clue.text: Work and play in Hampshire town

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as in 'the engine won't go'
sport means play or recreation

explanation.surface: A town on the south coast offers both employment and recreation.
explanation.walkthrough: Gosport is a naval town on the Solent in Hampshire, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a town opposite Portsmouth in Hampshire.

clue.text: Quietly intercepts forward pass

indicators.note: intercepts means the quiet letter cuts into the other word

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
P, piano, is the music abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: A football defender silently cuts out a pass aimed upfield.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is football, but 'pass' is the verb, as in pass the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend time is to pass it.

clue.text: Man an island? Not entire of itself!

indicators.note: not entire means the island's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: A twist on Donne: 'No man is an island, entire of itself'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes John Donne. STAFFA is an island off Mull in western Scotland; lose its last A for STAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To staff something is to man it with workers.

clue.text: Time superhero finally killed America's enemies — naturally

parts.note: He-Man is the muscle-bound hero of the Masters of the Universe cartoons

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word killed

parts.note: US, the United States, is America

explanation.surface: In time a comic-book strongman wipes out America's foes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase for a divided, us-against-the-enemy outlook, which 'naturally' signals as taken for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sets one's own side against opponents, viewing others as foes.

clue.text: Horse, initially headstrong, trotted round sign

indicators.note: round means the whole run of letters is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A wilful horse trotted around a signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes H and T; with MARE that is MAREHT, which 'round' turns to give the star sign Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Little creatures, caught out, unable to be beaten on course

definitions.text: unable to be beaten on course

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is removed

parts.note: dormice are small rodents
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Small animals are trapped and then escape, uncatchable on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught out' looks like trapped, but it says remove C (cricket's caught).
explanation.definitionFit: In golf matchplay, a player leading by as many holes as remain cannot lose the match.

clue.text: Working man adored princess

indicators.note: working suggests reshaping material, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A labourer worshipped a royal lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges MAN and ADORED.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was an Ethiopian princess rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: In divided city one restricted from crossing

indicators.note: restricted from means the letters are confined within the following word

explanation.surface: A resident of a partitioned city is barred from crossing the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The divided city is Berlin, and an Ossi is an East German; the four letters sit within 'crossing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossi is German slang for an East German, an Easterner of divided Berlin.

clue.text: Trunk and roots damaged

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk and its roots have been harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' fits the tree picture but means the body's middle; 'damaged' rearranges ROOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.

clue.text: Plant not in use -old country losing millions

parts.note: free means unoccupied or available

indicators.note: losing means the letter for millions is removed

parts.note: Siam is the old name of Thailand

explanation.surface: An unused garden plant from a former kingdom loses its millions.
explanation.walkthrough: SIAM, the former name of Thailand, loses M to give SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant of the iris family.

clue.text: Son enters sex club first (he pretends to be ignorant)

indicators.note: first says the golf club comes at the front

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: enters means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A young man joins a sex club first, feigning innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex club' reads as one venue; the words split, the golf club put 'first' and the son entering the word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironist uses irony, feigning ignorance like Socrates.
